clue.text: James's seamstress, Pinnie: one leaving tiny pens all over the place

indicators.note: scattered all over the place, so the letters of the two words are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I, which leaves the jumbled letters

explanation.surface: A seamstress drops tiny pins and pens all over her workroom floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' signals that the letters of TINY PENS are rearranged, and 'one leaving' says an I is taken away from that pool; the remaining letters spell the seamstress's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Amanda Pynsent, nicknamed Pinnie, is the dressmaker who brings up Hyacinth Robinson in The Princess Casamassima.

clue.text: Ring" cut short after China limits revolutionary composer

indicators.note: after puts the shortened word for ring behind the rest
limits means borders on all sides, so the friend surrounds the revolutionary

parts.note: in rhyming slang china (plate) means mate, a pal
Che Guevara was a revolutionary

indicators.note: cut short means losing the final letter

parts.note: a bell rings, and to ring is to bell

explanation.surface: A truncated ring sounds after China hems in a revolutionary composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is rhyming slang: china plate means mate, so PAL. 'cut short' turns BELL into BEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Pachelbel was a Baroque German composer, best known for his Canon in D.

clue.text: Romulus' grandpa is into rum unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The founder of Rome's grandfather has taken to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges INTO RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman legend Numitor, king of Alba Longa, was the grandfather of Romulus and Remus.

clue.text: Poet's village fire, finally caught, smothered by a fireman

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word for fire is taken

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: smothered by means covered over, so the fireman's letters surround the catch

parts.note: a stoker tends a furnace or boiler fire
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A fire in a village is finally contained when a fireman smothers it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fireman' is not a firefighter but someone who stokes a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: East Coker is the Somerset village of T. S. Eliot's ancestors and the title of one of his Four Quartets.

clue.text: Old city tax for the auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the word for tax is heard rather than read

parts.note: to tax is to tire or weary

explanation.surface: An ancient city levies a tax for its accountants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditors' looks like accountants but means listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyre was an ancient Phoenician port city, now in Lebanon.

clue.text: The Portobello Road ghost's taunts

definitions.meaning: in Muriel Spark's story The Portobello Road the narrator is a ghost nicknamed Needle; with the possessive
provocations or goads, as in jibes that needle someone

explanation.surface: A phantom haunting a London market street jeers at passers-by.
explanation.walkthrough: The ghost's nickname comes from finding a needle in a haystack as a child; with the possessive it gives the same letters as the plural noun for jibes. Portobello Road is a London street famous for its market.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle is to provoke, so needles are provoking remarks or jibes.

clue.text: Light used by novel lover, good and modern

parts.note: novel means new
a fan is a lover or devotee
LED is a light-emitting diode, a light

explanation.surface: A lamp is used by someone who loves a good modern novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' comes first in the clue but its letters come last: 'used by' puts it after the novel lover and good.
explanation.definitionFit: Newfangled describes something novel and up to date, often disapprovingly.

clue.text: Who raised Samuel as a prophet

parts.note: the priest Eli brought up the boy Samuel in the temple at Shiloh
taken as written

explanation.surface: Samuel's guardian brought him up to be a prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who raised Samuel' is not the definition but the priest ELI; the prophet comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Elias is the Greek form of Elijah, the Old Testament prophet.

clue.text: Mass, musical work by Disraeli

parts.note: a lot is a mass or large amount
Hair is the 1960s rock musical

explanation.surface: A Mass, a musical piece and a work by Disraeli.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' with a capital suggests the church service; it means a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothair is Benjamin Disraeli's 1870 novel.

clue.text: Irish playwright heard in carol recital

indicators.note: heard means the word is listened to, not seen

parts.note: to carol is to sing, and a recital is performed

explanation.surface: An Irish playwright is heard among the singers at a carol concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard in' signals that the playwright's name is spoken like the verb for carolling.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Synge wrote The Playboy of the Western World for Dublin's Abbey Theatre.

clue.text: Clubs wrestling over Milton's work

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

indicators.note: over signals that the word for wrestling is turned around end to end

parts.note: sumo is the Japanese style of wrestling

explanation.surface: A golf club's members try some wrestling, a work Milton never wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs wrestling' paints a fight, but Clubs is just the card-suit letter; Comus is Milton's masque.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton wrote the masque Comus, first performed at Ludlow Castle in 1634.

clue.text: In a new draft about an architect, keeping it tense

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the architect's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Sir Christopher Wren was the architect of St Paul's Cathedral
taken as written
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A biography of an architect gets revised, the author holding it in the present tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective for the writer's mood, but it is the grammar abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something composed again in a fresh version, revised, is in a new draft.

clue.text: Part apprentices lead on

indicators.note: only part of the next word is used, so the answer lies inside its letters

explanation.surface: Some trainees take the lead in a task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' points to letters inside apprENTICEs.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure or tempt someone is to lead them on.

clue.text: Hawthorne's novel energy after nuts and fruit

indicators.note: after says the energy symbol comes later than the nuts and fruit

parts.note: nuts as in enthusiasts, fans of something
a haw is the fruit of the hawthorn
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A novel by Hawthorne promises a burst of energy after eating nuts and fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' is not food here but enthusiasts; HAW, the hawthorn berry, neatly echoes the author's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanshawe, published anonymously in 1828, was Nathaniel Hawthorne's first novel.

clue.text: Duke in Europe is beaten by a king

indicators.note: beaten as in whisked or battered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: by as in multiplication, 3 by 4, written as the times sign X

explanation.surface: A duke in Europe is defeated by a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only says where the duke stands before 'beaten' scrambles the lot; 'by' is the multiplication sign, as in 3 by 4, and 'a king' translates the play's Latin title.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles' play title means King Oedipus, the Theban king who killed his father.

clue.text: Who helped Deborah save a king?

parts.note: save in the sense except, as does bar
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A question about who assisted a woman in rescuing a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like rescue, but it means except, giving BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Judges the commander Barak leads Israel's army alongside the prophetess Deborah.

clue.text: Keenness to value the Innocent Traveller's Topaz

parts.note: an edge is sharpness or keenness
worth is value

explanation.surface: A traveller's gem is assessed for its sharpness and value.
explanation.walkthrough: Topaz looks like a gemstone, but it is the heroine of Ethel Wilson's novel The Innocent Traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel Wilson's novel follows the long life of its heroine, Topaz Edgeworth.

clue.text: A dramatist's way to dismiss a singer: "bluesy, occasionally"

indicators.note: to dismiss means to send away, so the article is dropped from the word for route

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
Cher is a pop singer

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: A playwright has a way of dismissing a singer as only occasionally bluesy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dismiss a' drops the A from WAY; 'occasionally' takes LEY from bLuEsY.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wycherley was a Restoration playwright, author of The Country Wife.

clue.text: An Ephesian heretic's humane, yes, but wrong

indicators.note: wrong means not right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An early heretic is kind, yes, but mistaken in doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges HUMANE YES.
explanation.definitionFit: Hymenaeus is named in Paul's letters to Timothy as a heretic who had strayed from the faith.

clue.text: A flyer penned by the French poet

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the article surrounds the other letters

parts.note: le is French for the
taken as written
a martin is a bird, a flyer

explanation.surface: A leaflet written by the French poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A flyer' reads as a leaflet, but the flyer is a bird; 'the French' supplies the French article as the wrapper.
explanation.definitionFit: Alphonse de Lamartine was a leading French Romantic poet.

clue.text: Blend a drink for the Makar's Squyer

parts.note: to meld is to blend
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Mix a drink for the Scottish poet's squire.
explanation.walkthrough: A Makar is a Scots poet; Sir David Lyndsay wrote The Historie of Squyer Meldrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyndsay's poem tells of the adventures of William Meldrum, his squire hero.

clue.text: Capulet's first act, clumsily restricting Romeo's entrance

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the family name is taken
restricting means hemming in, so the clumsy acting surrounds another letter

parts.note: to ham is to overact clumsily
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Capulet stumbles about the stage, blocking Romeo as he comes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' looks like the noun for Romeo's arrival, but it is the verb meaning to delight; Romeo is just R.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to captivate or bewitch them.

clue.text: Lover who's abandoned song prior to uplifting finale

indicators.note: prior to puts the song in front of the rest

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song

indicators.note: uplifting in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a finale is the end

explanation.surface: A lover deserted sings a song before an uplifting ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' reverses END to DNE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Ariadne helped Theseus escape the labyrinth and was abandoned by him on Naxos.

clue.text: Country shielding one lord from Cymbeline

indicators.note: shielding means protecting from all sides, so the country surrounds the letter

parts.note: Belarus is a country in Eastern Europe
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A country gives sanctuary to a nobleman from Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shielding' puts I inside BELARUS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cymbeline, Belarius is the banished nobleman who raises the king's sons in Wales.

clue.text: Support's small for a corrupt lawyer

parts.note: bras are supports, and the possessive adds the S

explanation.surface: Bribery props up a crooked lawyer, but only on a small scale.
explanation.walkthrough: Sampson Brass is the crooked lawyer in Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Sampson Brass is an unscrupulous attorney in The Old Curiosity Shop.

clue.text: Lead in charge of some characters

parts.note: to run is to lead or manage
IC means in charge

explanation.surface: A leader in charge of some characters in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' suggests people in a story but means letters, the runes.
explanation.definitionFit: Runic letters belong to the old Germanic alphabet of runes.

clue.text: Hesse's story is, in retrospect, entitled to adopt the first person

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking backwards, so the whole built word is read from its end
to adopt means to take in, so the word for entitled swallows the pronoun

parts.note: named, given a title
I is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: Hesse's tale, looking back, gives its narrator a title and a voice of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to adopt' puts I inside NAMED to make NAIMED, and 'in retrospect' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Demian is Hermann Hesse's 1919 novel of a young man's awakening.

clue.text: Change course after being upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a tide is a course or flow

explanation.surface: Alter direction after a capsize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change course' looks like a phrase but 'course' is wordplay, TIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to revise or alter a text.

clue.text: Work by Lawrence's amazing staff

definitions.meaning: a novel by D. H. Lawrence, published 1922
the miraculous rod of Moses' brother that budded and turned into a serpent

explanation.surface: Lawrence's work is praised by his amazing staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' suggests employees, but it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical high priest's miraculous rod gave its name to Lawrence's novel.

clue.text: A "campus" novelist's room

definitions.meaning: David ..., author of the campus novels Changing Places and Nice Work
a ... is a small house or room, such as a porter's ...

explanation.surface: A writer of university novels has a room of his own.
explanation.definitionFit: A porter's or gatekeeper's lodge is a small room or cabin, and David Lodge is a famous campus novelist.

clue.text: A number holding firm after politician reveals blind man as a fake

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the number surrounds the other letters

parts.note: six is a number

indicators.note: after puts the firm's letters behind the politician's

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A number of people in a firm, after a politician exposes them, reveal a sham blind man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like an adjective but is a company; Simpcox is the sham-miracle beggar of Shakespeare's Henry VI Part 2.
explanation.definitionFit: In Henry VI Part 2 Simpcox pretends that a miracle has cured his blindness and is exposed as a fraud.

clue.text: Badly hurt? Yes, Mark Antony had him whipped

indicators.note: badly means done wrong, so the letters of the two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A servant asks if he is badly hurt after Antony orders his whipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' looks like part of the question but signals rearranging HURT YES.
explanation.definitionFit: In Antony and Cleopatra, Antony orders Caesar's messenger Thyreus to be whipped.
